title: Dataclass-first streaming schema adapters and validation utilities for Python SDK
creator: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: we want a predictable, ergonomic way for application teams to consume typed responses from the Python SDK across both eager and streaming responses while preferring native dataclasses for lightweight models. Current code paths are scattered between ad-hoc dict parsing, pydantic models used in some PRs, and multiple streaming helpers that don't expose a single typed interface. This ticket will deliver a dataclass-first approach with adapter utilities to interoperate with existing pydantic-based validators, plus a streaming wrapper that incrementally yields validated dataclass instances from chunked model output (partial JSON, newline-delimited JSON, and mixed text + JSON chunks). Goals: 1) Provide DataclassModel base and small runtime helpers for safe construction from nested JSON; 2) Add adapters that convert pydantic models <-> dataclasses so we can reuse existing validators without coupling new callers to pydantic; 3) Implement a robust streaming parser that buffers incomplete JSON fragments, yields typed objects as they become available, and exposes clear error semantics for partial failures; 4) Surface retry-safe hooks for streaming retries (idempotency tokens, resume offsets) and guidance for callers on when to retry vs. fail; 5) Ship minimal example notebook and unit/e2e tests to demonstrate migration and performance characteristics.
acceptance_criteria: A DataclassModel base type exists with helper constructors from dicts and JSON strings and documented limitations
Adapter utilities convert an existing pydantic model to the dataclass representation and back with round-trip tests
Streaming iterator API (stream_to_dataclass) accepts an async/iterable[bytes|str] and yields validated dataclass instances as they parse
Streaming parser handles: partial JSON chunks, NDJSON lines, and single JSON objects split across token boundaries in unit tests
Behavior on parse error is documented and tests cover configurable strategies: drop, fail, or emit RawChunk wrapper
Examples added: minimal script, Jupyter notebook, and README section demonstrating migration from freeform dicts to typed dataclasses
Performance regression within +/-5% for common prompt sizes vs current untyped streaming helpers in microbenchmarks
implementation_notes: Create packages/redwood_sdk/typing/dataclasses.py with DataclassModel helpers and safe_from_dict(cls, mapping) factory
Add adapters in packages/redwood_sdk/typing/adapters.py: pydantic_to_dataclass(model_instance) and dataclass_to_pydantic(dataclass_instance, pydantic_cls)

Streaming parser in packages/redwood_sdk/stream/parsers.py: small incremental JSON buffer using a character-level state machine to avoid heavy deps; fallback to python stdlib json.loads when a complete object is buffered
Expose async and sync convenience wrappers (sync wraps iterator with anyio.run) to match current SDK ergonomics
Retry hooks: stream iterator yields (item, resume_token) tuples; resume_token is opaque string generated from byte offset + last-full-object-hash
Add typed exceptions: StreamParseError, SchemaValidationError, ResumeTokenError with helpful message and attributes
Add top-level example under examples/python/typed_streaming_dataclasses.ipynb and a minimal CLI example in examples/python/typed_streaming_demo.py
migration_plan: Phase 1: land DataclassModel and adapters behind feature flag use_dataclass_models (internal default off)
Phase 2: wire streaming wrapper into internal example and opt-in SDK sample templates; collect feedback from SDK users/SEs
Phase 3: flip default to on for new minor release and publish migration guide with mapping patterns from dicts/pydantic to dataclasses
Provide compatibility layer for customer code using pydantic validators via adapters so they can migrate incrementally
tests: Unit tests for DataclassModel safe construction, required/optional field handling, and nested lists/dicts
Streaming unit tests simulating chunk boundaries inside object keys, deep nested objects, and NDJSON streams
Round-trip conversion tests pydantic <-> dataclass for a representative set of existing SDK models
Integration test that hooks the streaming wrapper into the local dev runtime and verifies resume_token correctness after simulated disconnects
Benchmarks to check overhead: small (<=128 tokens), medium (<=1024 tokens), and large streams
rollout_plan: Merge behind feature flag, ship internal alpha to SDK power users and collect telemetry for parsing errors and resume token usage
Monitor SDK telemetry for increased exceptions and latency for first two weeks after enabling default in staging
Publish migration docs and examples in the SDK repo and release notes for python-sdk-2.8
Coordinate with developer experience to update sample templates in the quickstart
